item.title: Israel’s Knesset Elects Kahana as Speaker to Boost Netanyahu Rivals
item.description: Israel’s parliament elected Matan Kahana, a member of Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party, as speaker in a move set to bolster lawmakers seeking to repeal Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s core legislation after last month’s inconclusive election.
item.dc:creator: Jon Herskovitz

item.title: Trump, Xi, World Leaders Gather in China for APEC: Live News and Updates
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Thailand Sees New US Chip Curbs as Threat to Ambitions to Be Data Center Hub
item.description: New US restrictions on the export and use of high-end semiconductors risk denting Thailand’s ambitions to be a hub for data centers, according to its top diplomat.
item.dc:creator: Haslinda Amin and Ramsey Al-Rikabi

item.title: Nvidia: Fiscal 2028 Revenue To Grow 75%
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Senate Homeland Security Chairman Rand Paul says he has not seen intelligence confirming that Alice Huang - the former Megaspeed executive linked to Jensen Huang and at the center of the Nvidia scandal - was a Chinese spy. Sen. Thom Tillis, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, says President Trump would be better served if Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick stepped aside, citing concerns over his judgment in the Nvidia fallout and beyond. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Singapore Urges Deeper Asean Ties in AI, Energy as 2027 Chair
item.description: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong called for deeper Asean integration in areas including finance, digital technologies and energy as the country is set to assume chairmanship of the regional bloc next year.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Lua

item.title: Sen. Tillis: Trump Better Served if Lutnick Moves On
item.description: Sen. Thom Tillis, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, says President Trump would be better served if Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick stepped aside, citing concerns over his judgment in the Nvidia fallout and beyond. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Takaichi Speaks With Trump Ahead of US-China-Russia Meeting
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi held one-on-one talks with US President Donald Trump on the sidelines of an international conference in Manila, Japan said, seeking to reaffirm strong ties before the US leader meets with his Chinese and Russian counterparts later this week.
item.dc:creator: Sakura Murakami

item.title: FCC Nominee Reviewed Skydance Pledge, Contrary to Testimony
item.description: A nominee to serve on the Federal Communications Commission played a small role in reviewing the merger between Skydance Media and Paramount Global, contradicting testimony she delivered to Congress last week, according to Senator Ben Ray Lujan.
item.dc:creator: Kelcee Griffis

item.title: Senator Rand Paul on Chip Exports, AI and FAA Ground Stop
item.description: US Senator Rand Paul, a Republican from Kentucky and chairman of the Senate Homeland Security Committee, discusses US-China technology tensions, national security concerns and public trust in government. Speaking on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition," Senator Paul raises concerns about potential conflicts of interest involving administration officials’ investments, predicts a booming market in “AI defense” firms to counter rogue AI and comments on the nationwide FAA ground stop. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Take: New AI Chip Limits Put Trump-Xi APEC Meeting in Focus
item.description: New limits on remote AI chips and servers will impact Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping talks at the APEC summit. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s Push to Reopen US Doors to Chinese Investment Faces Roadblocks
item.description: Trump’s efforts to reopen the US’s doors to Chinese investment have run into a problem partly of his own making. A Bloomberg News analysis of 137 deals that faced review shows the obstacles have multiplied, going beyond sensitive tech companies.
item.dc:creator: Lucille Liu, Nectar Gan, Jenny Leonard, Yasufumi Saito and Spe Chen

item.title: No Intel Confirms Alice Huang Was a Chinese Say, Says Sen. Paul
item.description: Senate Homeland Security Chairman Rand Paul, a Republican from Kentucky, says he has not seen intelligence confirming that Alice Huang - the former Megaspeed executive linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang - was a Chinese spy. He also raises questions about how to modernize the FAA and ownership of the agency’s fiber-optic network in an interview with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Nvidia Earnings Beat
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Nvidia reports earnings for the first time since Jensen Huang’s surprise departure, putting the chipmaker’s 70% growth outlook and the broader AI trade back in focus. The chipmaker gave a sales forecast that exceeded Wall Street estimates, signaling that demand remains strong following the chaotic exit of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.
On today’s episode:
Dina Bass, Bloomberg News AI Infrastructure Reporter Jay Goldberg, Senior Analyst, Semiconductors & Electronics, Seaport Research Partners Kunjan Sobhani, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Semiconductor Analyst Christopher Beam, Bloomberg Businessweek Senior Writer Laura Rippy, Managing Partner at Alumni Ventures (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Venezuela Lawmakers Back $26.6 Billion Public Borrowing Bill
item.description: Venezuela’s National Assembly took a first step toward passing a bill that would allow the government to take on up to $26.6 billion in additional in debt.
item.dc:creator: Andreina Itriago and Fabiola Zerpa

item.title: Trump Agrees to Deposition by Jan. 22 in $10 Billion BBC Suit
item.description: A judge in Florida agreed to give President Donald Trump an extra six weeks to sit for a mandatory deposition in the $10 billion defamation suit he filed against the British Broadcasting Corp., with a new deadline of Jan. 22.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson

item.title: Prediction Markets Create Legions of ‘Problem Gamblers’
item.description: Bloomberg’s Aaron Gordon joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Crypto.” They discuss this year’s massive surge in prediction markets use due to the World Cup over the summer and the recent US midterm elections. Prediction market companies have effectively brought gambling to all 50 states. Bloomberg took a deep-dive into the data behind the betting surge. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Fed Games Out How AI Could Reshape Work and the Economy
item.description: Staffers are looking at scenarios from boom to bust.
item.dc:creator: Enda Curran

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 11/17/2026
item.description: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed willingness to return to the helm after his dramatic ouster last week, though the board isn’t currently considering such an idea. The company cut ties with Huang after the revelation that he’d had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who is now under investigation for potentially spying on behalf of China. Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter Ian King joins to discuss. Then, Howard Capital Management CEO and Portfolio Manager Vance Howard weighs in on market reaction to Huang’s ouster. Plus, Bloomberg Businessweek Senior Writer Christopher Beam discusses his latest story on AI entrepreneurs in China. Finally, Laura Rippy, Managing Partner at Alumni Ventures, weighs in on how Anthropic’s IPO could impact the VC landscape. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CFTC Orders Kalshi to Take Down Markets on Trump’s Speeches
item.description: Federal regulators ordered Kalshi Inc. to halt trading on markets tied to what President Donald Trump will say during public events, in the latest sign that prediction markets are coming under greater scrutiny after the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Bobby Allyn

item.title: Latvian Leader Kulbergs Wins Parliament Backing for New Cabinet
item.description: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs won a parliamentary approval for his new government as he tapped people with no prior experience in politics for the most prominent jobs in the administration.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Eglitis
